facts.text: Calvin University was founded in 1876 and named for 16th-century reformer John Calvin, and is united in a covenantal relationship with the Christian Reformed Church in North America.

sources.title: Who We Are - About Calvin | Calvin University
sources.quote: Calvin University was founded in 1876 and named for 16th-century reformer John Calvin. While retaining a separate identity and function, the university is united in a covenantal relationship with the Christian Reformed Church in North America.

facts.text: A partnership between Calvin University and Calvin Theological Seminary, the Calvin Prison Initiative provides a Christian liberal arts education to incarcerated individuals at the Richard A. Handlon Correctional Facility in Ionia, MI, where enrolled students do not pay the cost of tuition, textbooks, or computers.

sources.title: Calvin Prison Initiative | Calvin University
sources.quote: A partnership between Calvin University and Calvin Theological Seminary, the Calvin Prison Initiative (CPI) provides a Christian liberal arts education to incarcerated individuals at the Richard A. Handlon Correctional Facility in Ionia, MI.

sources.title: Calvin Prison Initiative | Calvin University
sources.quote: The enrolled students do not pay the cost of tuition, textbooks, or computers. These costs are covered by the Calvin Prison Initiative, which is funded through donations and grants.
